method: Personally inspected all nine actual 390x844 unlettered history screenshots, full native framing. This is source art review; final BP lettering is separately pending. Parent preliminary art observations were disclosed before native inspection; independent assessment is not blinded.

observations: At 338px art width the old cream wallet handoff and restrained resentment remain clear. The receiving hand is visibly bare, preserving the glove-state discontinuity; barred gate differs from NG13 solid panel. City glints remain busy but faces dominate.

New black sealed letter and old cream belt wallet are distinguishable at phone size. Both gloves return. Pell and Aren attention produces an effective hook exchange; fine city details remain secondary.
Neris hands behind glass, Ilyra back and left silver guard, and threshold root all read at phone size. Fine red ground and glass patina compete without erasing the trapped-person stakes.

Narrow open door and root tip withdrawn from threshold remain visible. The tip nearly touches the red ground, so a large clean airborne clearance is not established. This is a usable but modest rule demonstration.

Giant translucent petal silhouette and small armed heroine give a strong threatening scale contrast. Planted root at the right threshold is visible. Still image alone does not establish the stamping motion; red ground and vein webbing remain dense.

Crouched face, right saber, left guard, torn coat and distant captive remain identifiable at phone size. Root snakes to the right doorway while Neris is in the left background glass; room geography remains less certain than the emotional choice.

Braced backswing and intact root are readable, but fine interior detail competes with the small figure. Root is already out on open floor here; BP11 alone is not the cause of the threshold geography discontinuity.

Boot, loose cut piece at doorway, opening door and Neris stepping out remain legible together at phone size. Fallen flower supports the consequence. This practical rescue payoff lowers the case for an isolated BP11 repair; coat tear is not clearly retained.

Left guarded hand picking up the packet and right lowered saber remain clear. The clue seal is small and ornate rather than a plainly resolved broken leaf. Fallen petals and red carpet compete with the pickup but do not conceal it.

limits: No owner approval or human comfort/comprehension result.
No new structural priority above previously documented RC01 duplicate cast and NG08 staging; BP12 outcome is materially readable despite prior root geography and saber-side errors.
